claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says: Further details have emerged about two police officers hailed for preventing a Polish gunman from killing more.
- Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt: Several carriages derailed after two trains travelling in the same direction crashed outside the city of Giza.
- Homes and temples glow across India to mark Diwali: Millions of Indians are marking the festival of lights with glowing lamps, fireworks and traditional sweets.
- Cruise ship pianist rescued from sea after nine hours in Pacific Ocean: Two US fishermen say they spotted the man treading water around 20 miles (32km) off the Californian coast.
- Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes: Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows damage to the building in the capital's central financial district.
- 'Flat', 'tired', 'cynical': Unusually gloomy Kiwis deliver New Zealand's tightest election in years: The national mood is low, and faith in politics even lower - with voters deserting the major parties at the polls.
- Iran executes three men for 'armed unrest' after January protests: It is claimed Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were part of anti-government protests earlier this year.
- 'I treat all these people like they are victims', says doctor who treated Krakow shooting suspect: Two doctors were eating near the Polish city's Main Market Square when a gunman began firing at random.
- Footage shows derailed carriages after fatal train crash in Egypt: At least seven people died when two trains collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment.
- How the deadly shooting in Krakow unfolded: Video authenticated by BBC Verify shows the moment gunshots rang out in Krakow's main market square.
- Gaza wedding festival sees 250 couples married at the same time: A mass wedding for Palestinian brides and grooms has taken place in the rubble-strewn streets of Gaza.
- Watch: Is it the end of the road for Tesla's Cybertruck?: The car company's CEO Elon Musk has said production will halt in Texas, to focus on the firm's self-driving Cybercabs.
